name: The Fig Tree of the Huerto del Rey Moro

location.address: Huerto del Rey Moro, Calle Enladrillada 36, 41003 Sevilla

access: Free, open daily as a self-managed community garden; entrance on Calle Enladrillada 36.
transport: In the Casco Antiguo near the Macarena walls, about a 10 minute walk from Puerta de la Macarena, served by TUSSAM bus lines including C4.
verified_sources: Inventario de Arboles Singulares de la Ciudad de Sevilla (2022), Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, ficha 17
verify_notes: Access confirmed independently of the catalogue: huertodelreymoro.org (the garden's own site) describes it as the largest public, non-commercialised open space in Seville's historic centre, free entry, self-managed by and for the neighbourhood since 2004, on the site of a domestic plot attached to the former Casa del Rey Moro (late 15th/early 16th century). The garden's own site states the fig is 'more than 300 years old', which is the source of age_estimate here; treat it as a vague, real-source age and do not sharpen it further. Catalogue condition ratings: estado fisiologico Estresado (stressed), fitosanitario Sin anomalias, biomecanico Comprometido, conservacion Regular. None of that is a reason to hold it back per the project's own rule that condition ratings are not a publication gate. Girth 147 cm at 1.30 m, 300 cm at the base; crown 9.5 m. The garden itself, not just the tree, is worth a line in the story: it is a well-known piece of Seville's urban-commons history, squatted and defended by neighbours against demolition, which gives the fig a genuine backstory beyond its age.

name: The Stone Pine of the Jardines de Cristina
access: Free, open public city garden at all hours; between Puerta de Jerez and the river.
transport: At Puerta de Jerez, about 2 minutes' walk from the Puerta de Jerez Metrocentro tram stop (line T1).
verified_sources: Inventario de Arboles Singulares de la Ciudad de Sevilla (2022), Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, ficha 33
verify_notes: Second, independent source: Asociacion Amigos de los Jardines de la Oliva's own piece on Seville's singular trees names this specific pine (parterre 15 of the Jardines de Cristina) as dating from the period the garden was inaugurated as the Salon de Cristina on 24 July 1830 by Queen Maria Cristina, under corregidor/asistente Jose Manuel de Arjona. This is a source naming THIS tree, not just the garden's founding date, so it is used as a specimen-level estimate rather than a bridge claim: 1830 to 2026 is about 196 years, given here as a broad band (180-210) rather than a false-precise figure. Catalogue condition: fisiologico Normal, fitosanitario Sin anomalias, biomecanico Comprometido, conservacion Regular; girth 280 cm at 1.30 m, 311 cm at base, crown 12.5 m. The gardens themselves are one of Seville's older public green spaces, an 8,100 sq m plot between the historic Puerta de Jerez and the Guadalquivir, established 1830, so the pine has stood through the garden's whole public life.

name: The Multi-Stemmed Palm of the Conde de Colombi

location.address: Parque de María Luisa, Avenida de Conde de Colombi, 41013 Sevilla
location.neighbourhood: El Prado-Parque de María Luisa, Sur

access: Free, inside the public Parque de María Luisa, open daily.
transport: Inside Parque de María Luisa near Plaza de España, about a 10 minute walk from the Prado de San Sebastián bus and tram interchange.
verified_sources: Inventario de Arboles Singulares de la Ciudad de Sevilla (2022), Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, ficha 46
verify_notes: Single-sourced (catalogue only); access is not in question, it stands in Maria Luisa park, Seville's grand public park, where several other trees on our site already stand (thickens the existing cluster). Girth not given at 1.30 m (girth_130_cm recorded 'No aplica' since the trunk forks low into multiple stems); base girth 875 cm across the multiple trunks, so record that figure only as a multi-stem measurement, never as a single-trunk girth. Height 15.8 m, mean crown 11.5 m. Condition: fisiologico Normal, fitosanitario Sin anomalias, biomecanico Normal, conservacion Regular. What makes it singular per the catalogue's own naming is the multi-caule (multi-trunked) growth habit, unusual for a date palm, which normally grows as a single trunk; worth leading the story with that oddity rather than age, since none is documented. No age basis found; leave the field asking the reader.

name: The Harp Eucalyptus of the Guadalquivir

location.address: Anillo Verde, Ribera del Río Guadalquivir, 41011 Sevilla

access: Free, on the public riverside path and cycle route of the Anillo Verde (Green Ring), open at all times.
transport: On the Guadalquivir riverside path in Tablada; nearest useful stop is around Avda. Maestranza Aerea, roughly a 15 to 20 minute walk to the riverbank, or reach it by bike via the segregated riverside cycle path that runs the length of the Guadalquivir.
verified_sources: Inventario de Arboles Singulares de la Ciudad de Sevilla (2022), Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, ficha 44
verify_notes: Single-sourced (catalogue only). Access confirmed by general knowledge of the site rather than a second named source: the Anillo Verde/Corredor Verde Metropolitano along the Guadalquivir is a public, signposted green corridor with a continuous segregated bike and pedestrian path (Sevilla's riverside cycle route, part of one of Spain's most developed urban cycling networks), open ground with no gate. This stretch is somewhat out of the way, in Tablada on the west bank south of the city centre, more a bike or long-walk destination than a stroll from downtown; say so honestly rather than implying it is central. Girth 300 cm measured 3 m up the trunk rather than at the standard 1.30 m (catalogue note: 'a 3 m de la base'), record that caveat so the writer does not present it as a standard chest-height girth. Height 18 m. Condition: fisiologico Normal, fitosanitario Sin anomalias, biomecanico Comprometido, conservacion Regular; carries the same two pests as several of Seville's other big river eucalyptus (Glycaspis brimblecombei, a sap-sucking psyllid, and Laetiporus sulphureus, chicken of the woods, a wood-decay fungus), both already documented on the published El Gran Capitan (sev_005) and El Eucalipto de Pedro Salinas (sev_031), so this may be worth a line about the same pest pressure affecting Seville's big river eucalyptus generally. No age documented; leave the field asking the reader.

name: The Grapefruit of the Cartuja Monastery

location.address: Huerta Grande, Monasterio de la Cartuja (CAAC), Isla de la Cartuja, 41092 Sevilla

access: Paid entry: inside the Monasterio de la Cartuja, now the Centro Andaluz de Arte Contemporaneo (CAAC), a public museum. A monument ticket and a combined monument-plus-exhibitions ticket are both sold at a few euros each; free entry runs Tuesday to Friday 19:00-21:00 and on Saturdays. Open Tuesday to Saturday 11:00-21:00, Sunday and holidays 10:00-15:30, closed Mondays. The self-guided route through the monastery ends at the old orchards, Huerta Vieja and Huerta Grande, so any visitor who buys a ticket during opening hours reaches the tree.
transport: On Isla de la Cartuja; TUSSAM bus lines C1 and C2 stop close by (Lopez Pintado/Caixa Forum, about 2 minutes' walk, or Americo Vespucio/Monasterio de la Cartuja, about 4 minutes' walk). Also reachable on foot from Triana over the Pasarela de la Cartuja footbridge.
verified_sources: Inventario de Arboles Singulares de la Ciudad de Sevilla (2022), Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, ficha 10
verify_notes: Access researched specifically because the site is a paid museum: confirmed the visit route explicitly includes the historic orchards (Huerta Vieja and Huerta Grande) as its final stretch, so this is not a restricted back area, it is on the standard visitor path. Ownership is Junta de Andalucia (titularidad in the catalogue), maintained by the monastery's own upkeep team. Girth 220 cm measured at 0.85 m rather than the standard 1.30 m (catalogue: 'perimetro a 0,85 m'), base girth 250 cm; height 14 m, crown 13 m. Condition: fisiologico Normal, fitosanitario Sin anomalias, biomecanico Normal, conservacion Regular. No age documented, and grapefruit (Citrus x paradisi) is itself a relatively recent hybrid, first recorded in Barbados in the 18th century, so a claim of great age would not be credible regardless; the story angle is the monastery's centuries-old tradition of monastic orchards (the Carthusians farmed this land from the 15th century) rather than the individual tree's age. Leave age fields empty.

name: The Lagunaria of the Jardines de la Madrina

location.address: Jardines de la Madrina, near the Casino de la Exposicion, 41013 Sevilla

access: Free, in the Jardines de la Madrina, a small city-run garden beside the Casino de la Exposicion. This is a separate, publicly accessible strip of the old San Telmo estate, not the same ground as the adjoining Palacio de San Telmo, whose own main gardens remain closed to the public and visitable only by appointment.
transport: Near Plaza de Espana and the Prado de San Sebastian bus and tram interchange, about a 10 minute walk.
verified_sources: Inventario de Arboles Singulares de la Ciudad de Sevilla (2022), Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, ficha 40
verify_notes: ACCESS WAS THE OPEN QUESTION HERE, now resolved: the catalogue's own emplazamiento reads 'Antiguos jardines de San Telmo (La Madrina)', which risks reading as the still-closed Palacio de San Telmo grounds (the palace itself is the seat of the Presidencia de la Junta de Andalucia and its principal gardens require an appointment, confirmed by a 2024 elespanol.com piece asking whether they will ever become a public park). But the Jardines de la Madrina are a DIFFERENT, smaller, already-public strip of the same historic Montpensier estate, near the Casino de la Exposicion and the Pabellon de Chile, restored as a public garden in 2013-2015 under the city's own Delegacion de Medio Ambiente. This is corroborated three ways: the catalogue's own titularidad for this tree is 'Ayto. de Sevilla' (city-owned) with gestion 'Seccion Medios Propios, Ayto. de Sevilla' (the city's own maintenance section), NOT Junta de Andalucia or the Presidencia, which is what owns/manages the still-closed part; two independent local-history sources (a 2015 Sevilla culture blog and an architecture blog on the same restoration) describe La Madrina as a distinct, recovered green space with its own pedestrian paths, separate from the palace; and the coordinates place it beside the Casino de la Exposicion rather than at the palace building itself. Do NOT present this as 'inside the Palacio de San Telmo', the story must say it is the adjoining public garden strip, and note the palace's own grounds are closed. Girth 275 cm at 1.30 m, 433 cm at base; height 22 m, mean crown 10.3 m. Condition: fisiologico Optimo, fitosanitario Sin anomalias, biomecanico Normal, conservacion Bueno, all good. UNRESOLVED AGE DISPUTE, flag for the writer: the catalogue implies this is among Seville's oldest lagunarias, but Asociacion Amigos de los Jardines de la Oliva's own singular-trees piece places the oldest lagunaria specimens in Seville at the Jardines de Cristina and the Real Alcazar, not here. Do not claim 'among the oldest' in the story; state only the measurements and let the age question stay open. Single independent source found for the access claim (two blogs on the same 2013-2015 restoration, arguably one story told twice), so still flagged for species/age per the normal single-catalogue-source rule.
